selection_note: UPSTREAM UPGRADE BATCH 18. Five previously unscreened distinct included S1=A/S2=C Index sources selected after all 17 integrated prior cohorts and visible open PR source claims were reconciled. Each hypothesis was prospectively preregistered in exact remote checkpoint commit 97273405215b8652073ddba5cfd222233c321328 before current external code, issues or PRs were inspected. Screening order is descending Index reviewed_at (wanman, cast, react-agent-harness, Genesis Agent, Orkas), not the thematic subsection order in the hypothesis note. All five are questions, not proven defects, and no external publication grant follows.

candidates.finding: Assessment S2=C observes first-party conflicting task/capsule scope admission and explicitly calls out possible concurrent admission races. Predict two overlapping TASK_CREATE RPC calls could both pass an unreserved scope check; falsify with serialized/atomic admission or a design that forbids the concurrent path.
candidates.observed_native_change: Independent dev-alpha-2 SSH host Zhdanov, native Node 22.23.4 / pnpm 9.15.0 / Vitest 4.1.4 in pinned node:22-bookworm-slim: source d3a8138 plus identical new first-party regression tests yielded 1 FAIL / 1 PASS before patch (both overlapping tasks wrongly admitted), 2 PASS after. Existing+new supervisor and TaskPool controls yielded 68/68 PASS after; runtime TypeScript typecheck PASS. Exact separate-runner command/session IDs and logs summarized in pilots/wanman-s2/INDEPENDENT_HOST_RECEIPT_2026-11-09.md. Only bounded admission correctness, not deployed benefit.

candidates.finding: Assessment S2=C observes a shared interactive confirmation queue across concurrent child agents. Predict an aborted or rejected predecessor could stall the sibling prompt queue; falsify if first-party serializer always recovers and progresses or abort cancels the whole parent by contract.
candidates.screening_result: Current first-party confirmation serializer explicitly absorbs rejection of the predecessor when updating confirmChain (run.then(success, failure)), yet returns the original run to the awaiting caller. A rejected earlier prompt does not poison the subsequent queue; original predicted stall is falsified by source. MIT; no matching new contribution justified. No native test, model or external write.

candidates.finding: Assessment S2=C observes per-task mutable agent clones that share a common run-wide budget. Predict simultaneous clones might both pass a stale remaining-budget admission and overspend the shared cap; falsify if charge/reservation is already atomic or budget intentionally advisory.
candidates.blocker: Concurrent ReAct task clones share BudgetGuard; check() reads cumulative cost before each model request while add_cost() accounts afterward. Source supports an advisory overshoot concern, but no first-party documented upper bound or safe pre-call reservation exists for unknown model cost. Need maintainer-backed budget semantics and an offline first-party native counterfactual before changing admission policy. MIT, no model/provider test or external write.

candidates.finding: Assessment S2=C observes thread-based skill-library write serialization and atomic JSON index replacement. Predict two independently supported processes sharing the library may both commit from stale snapshots and lose one skill; falsify if process sharing unsupported or cross-process synchronization already exists.
candidates.screening_result: Current first-party save_skill() already serializes same-thread updates under _SAVE_LOCK and cross-process index writes under locked(_index_path()); the pre-code lost-update prediction omitted an existing supported lock. MIT, no new change or native test justified; no model/provider/external write.

candidates.finding: Assessment S2=C observes path-keyed exclusive write/rename coordination among concurrent tool actors. Predict legal alias-equivalent output paths may take separate locks yet resolve to the same destination; falsify if canonical identity is used or aliases rejected by the supported first-party tool.
candidates.blocker: Current exclusive fileEditLock uses lexical path.resolve, whereas supported workspace symlink aliases may have equal physical destinations. The apparent alias-lock gap still lacks a safe first-party native concurrent write test and an established policy for alias-resolved write/rename; symlink existence, denied escapes and unrelated path-sandbox constraints must be distinguished. Need a deterministic supported write_tool fixture, documented counterfactual and maintainer policy before altering locking. MIT; no model/provider or external write.
